children: Taiwan will likely start raising its interest rate in December given strong corporate credit growth, robust wage increase and continued domestic consumption momentum, Goldman Sachs economists say in a note. The U.S. bank expects the Taiwan central bank to deliver three consecutive quarterly rate increases of 12.5 bps each starting in December. The economists expect this tightening cycle to be short, given prospects of a brief Fed tightening cycle followed by a potential resumption of rate cuts in the second half of 2027. Meanwhile, Taiwan's underlying cost pressures should gradually moderate, with headline inflation likely to fall back below the central bank's 2.0% threshold by 3Q 2027, Goldman Sachs says. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
